title: Grill — Add Fable 5.2 to the supported harnesses
summary:
Before this gets planned: **9 decisions** the build would otherwise make silently, plus **4 defaults** I'd bet on. Start with **harness scope**, **Mythos 5.2 parity** and the **default model** — those change the plan's shape. The confirm list at the end is one click each.

Source: the pipeline task title ("Add Fable 5.2 to the supported harnesses — Claude Code, primarily") plus `docs/plans/add-fable-5-2-investigation.md`. There is no external spec to commit.

proven.text: **Fable 5.2 is real in the installed Claude Code 2.1.321.** Its changelog and binary carry `claude-fable-5-2` as the default Fable model — 1M context, 128K output, $8/$40 per MTok, $0.20 cache reads, full low→max effort, thinking always on, API/CLI default effort medium. The `fable` alias resolves to 5.2.

**Cursor offers it in exactly five plain effort variants** — `claude-fable-5-2-{low,medium,high,xhigh,max}` — with no `-thinking-*` and no `-fast` ids. Every label contains `1M`, so max mode is inferred, not live-probed.

**fx has it in the public/unauth Gateway catalog but not in your signed-in catalog.** `HOME=<empty> fx models --json` and the public Gateway list `anthropic/claude-fable-5.2` (low→max, no toggle/none); your real signed-in catalog has 138 ids and **zero** `anthropic/*` ids. A curated fx row must therefore be `catalogOnly` and will be invisible on your account today.

**The other harnesses need nothing.** Copilot CLI 1.0.108 (published 2026-11-09) mentions Fable 5.1 and Fable 5, never 5.2, and its binary has no `claude-fable*` id. Antigravity 1.5.1 carries only Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini ids. OpenCode already lists `opencode/claude-fable-5-2` through discovery. Codex and Gemini run non-Anthropic models.

**There is no Claude Code data migration.** `task.model` is a free string: 227 tasks on `fable-5` and 84 on `fable-5.1` keep launching those models. Cursor has **zero** stored Fable variant rows in prod or dev, so migration 084 is data-clean on this machine and exists for future/other users.

**The load-bearing edit is the argv map.** Unknown model ids pass through verbatim, so without a `CLAUDE_MODEL_FLAG` entry the launched argv is `--model fable-5.2` instead of `--model claude-fable-5-2`.

**The pipeline config needs no change.** `AGENTS_CONFIG.yml` uses the alias `fable` (`model is opus | sonnet | haiku | fable`), and the installed CLI now resolves that alias to Fable 5.2 — cheaper than Fable 5.1 ($8/$40 vs $10/$50).

sections.title: Scope & targets
sections.intro: These three decide how much of the repo moves. The model facts are settled; these are product/scope calls.

questions.title: Which harnesses should get a curated Fable 5.2 row in this change?
questions.why: Each harness adds a different surface: Claude Code is the row/argv/effort/picker work; Cursor adds a spec + migration; fx adds a catalogOnly row plus count and e2e updates.
questions.context: Claude Code is required. Cursor's live catalog (2026.10.22) has five `claude-fable-5-2-{low,medium,high,xhigh,max}` rows. A `CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS` entry gives one row with an effort picker and max mode, and hides the five discovered rows. fx's public/unauth Gateway catalog has `anthropic/claude-fable-5.2`, but a `catalogOnly` row only appears when the harness's discovered catalog positively contains it — your signed-in catalog has zero `anthropic/*` ids, so it would be invisible to you today. OpenCode already lists the model through discovery.

questions.title: Add `mythos-5.2` alongside Fable 5.2, or leave the Mythos block at 5.1/5?
questions.why: The CLI ships Mythos 5.2 as Fable 5.2's org-gated twin. The task names only Fable 5.2, so this is a scope decision, not an evidence question.
questions.context: Claude Code 2.1.321's metadata has `claude-mythos-5-2` with the same price, context and effort as Fable 5.2, gated to approved orgs (Project Glasswing). No Cursor, fx, Copilot or Antigravity catalog carries any Mythos id, so a Mythos 5.2 row would be Claude Code-only. Today's top Mythos row is 5.1.

{ id: "mythos-5", label: "Mythos 5", hint: "Prior Mythos release — Fable 5's twin; …" },

options.label: Leave Mythos 5.2 out (owner-deferred)
options.description: Record it as a separate ticket in the completeness ledger.
options.consequence: Mythos 5.1 stays the newest Mythos row and still launches; Fable 5.2 becomes the newest Fable. No extra row, flag, effort/mode entry or tests.

options.label: Add `mythos-5.2` (Claude Code only)
options.description: `mythos-5.2` → `claude-mythos-5-2`, full effort ladder, `[]` mode deny, picker family `null`.
options.consequence: Restores newest-first Mythos parity; adds one row, one flag, one effort entry, one mode entry and ~4 test/comment updates.

recommendation.reason: The ticket is Fable 5.2; Mythos is org-gated and no other harness catalog carries it, so it is a clean separate decision.

questions.title: Keep Opus 5.5 as the Claude Code default, or make Fable 5.2 the default?
questions.why: A default flip changes what every new task runs and what it costs — Fable 5.2 is exactly 2× Opus 5.5's $4/$20.
questions.context: `DEFAULT_MODEL['claude-code']` is `opus-5.5`; the comment says the default stays on the most-capable non-premium tier because Fable/Mythos cost 2×. Your prod DB has 227 `fable-5` tasks and 84 `fable-5.1` tasks, so Fable is chosen deliberately, not by default. A flip also touches `e2e/agent-profiles-launch.spec.ts`, README:78 and the default comment.

evidence.label: current default and its rationale

options.label: Keep Opus 5.5
options.description: Fable 5.2 is one click away at the top of the Fable block.
options.consequence: No change to new-task cost; README, default tests and the profiles e2e stay untouched.

options.label: Make Fable 5.2 the default
options.description: Every new Claude Code task starts on the 2× premium tier.
options.consequence: Update `DEFAULT_MODEL`, the default-output test, `e2e/agent-profiles-launch.spec.ts`, README:78 and the default comments in the same wave.

recommendation.reason: Same house rule as the Fable 5.1 plan: premium 2× tiers stay opt-in; a flip is a separate product decision with a visible cost change.

sections.title: Picker placement & copy
sections.intro: The list is family-grouped, newest first. These decide where the new row sits and what the picker tells users about cost.

questions.title: Where should Fable 5.2 sit in the Claude Code picker?
questions.why: The order is the first thing users see; it also determines whether the row reads as the newest model or as one family's current release.
questions.context: Today: Mythos 5.1, Mythos 5, Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 5.5, … — family-grouped, newest first within each family. The prior Fable 5.1 plan explicitly chose family grouping, not global newest-first. Fable 5.2 is 'our most intelligent generally available model', but the Mythos tier sits above it (and is org-gated).

evidence.label: prior owner decision: family-grouped, newest first within family

options.label: Keep family grouping: Mythos 5.1, Mythos 5, Fable 5.2, Fable 5.1, Fable 5, Opus 5.5…
options.description: Fable 5.2 is the first row in the Fable block.
options.consequence: Consistent with every existing Claude row and the Fable 5.1 precedent; no other rows move.

options.label: Put Fable 5.2 at the very top, above Mythos
options.consequence: Breaks the family grouping and puts a generally available model above the org-gated tier; the Mythos block moves down one.

recommendation.reason: Matches the existing picker structure and the Fable 5.1 decision; the hint already says 'most capable widely released'.

questions.title: How should the Fable/Mythos hints change?
questions.why: The picker is the only place users see the 2× cost signal, and Fable 5.1 is now more expensive than Fable 5.2 relative to today's default Opus.
questions.context: Current hints: Fable 5.1 = 'Most capable widely released model — above Opus. Uses 2x the usage of Opus.'; Fable 5 = 'Prior Fable release — above Opus. Uses 2x…'; Mythos 5.1 = 'Fable 5.1's twin — same capability and cost… Uses 2x…'. Fable 5.2 is $8/$40 (2× Opus 5.5's $4/$20); Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are $10/$50 (2.5× Opus 5.5, though still 2× Opus 5 at $5/$25). Fable 5's current price was not re-verified, so it is left alone.

sections.title: Cursor data migration
sections.intro: Only relevant if Cursor is in scope. A spec entry 'covers' the five variant ids; stored variant rows need normalizing, per repo convention.

questions.title: Include Cursor migration 084 for the five Fable 5.2 variants?
questions.why: Adding the spec hides the five discovered rows. A stored variant id would then render unlisted with a collapsed effort picker. Migrations are one-way in this repo.
questions.context: Next free number is 084. The convention (055/056/060/062/064/076) is a kind-joined normalization into base id + effort + `speed='off'` for cursor-kind `tasks`, `agent_profiles` and `lastModel:cursor`, leaving `lastEffort:cursor`, `updated_at` and frozen snapshots alone. Prod and dev have zero `claude-fable-5-1-*` / `claude-fable-5-2-*` rows, so the migration is data-clean here; it protects future/other users.

evidence.label: 076 — the exact template (header + tasks/profile/preferences updates)
evidence.code:
-- Cursor: this release adds CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS entries for three new families …
-- Normalize to base id + effort, the shape cursorModelArg re-composes …
UPDATE tasks SET effort = substr(...), speed = 'off', model = '…'
WHERE model IN (…) AND agent IN (SELECT id FROM harnesses WHERE kind = 'cursor');

evidence.label: last registered migration is 083

options.label: Include 084 now
options.description: Five UPDATEs, kind-joined, idempotent, plus the migrate test.
options.consequence: Follows the 076 template; adds the migration file, index registration and a migrate.test pin. One-way, but no rows are mutated on this machine.

options.label: Skip the migration
options.description: No stored 5.2 variant data exists today.
options.consequence: Any user who picked a 5.2 variant before the spec lands gets an unlisted row + collapsed effort picker. Record as owner-deferred.

recommendation.reason: Every prior Cursor spec addition shipped its normalization migration; the cost is one SQL file + one test, and it is data-clean here.

questions.title: Should 084 also backfill the pre-existing Fable 5.1 plain variants?
questions.why: Fable 5.1's spec shipped without a normalization migration, so any stored plain 5.1 variant is already in the unlisted/collapsed state.
questions.context: The 5.1 spec covers `claude-fable-5-1-{max,xhigh,high,medium,low}`; its `-thinking-*` variants are intentionally uncovered. There is no 5.1 normalization migration in `src/bun/migrations`. Prod and dev have zero such rows today. Including it is one extra block in the same SQL file; leaving it out is a separate ticket.

evidence.label: Fable 5.1 Cursor spec — plain ids only
investigation: the 5.1 spec shipped without a migration

options.label: Backfill the five plain 5.1 variants in 084
options.description: One extra block in the same file; `-thinking-*` stays untouched.
options.consequence: Fixes the pre-existing gap in the same pass; adds test cases. Kind-joined and idempotent like the 5.2 block.

options.label: Leave 5.1 out; separate ticket
options.consequence: Any stored 5.1 plain variant stays unlisted until a later migration. Record as owner-deferred.

recommendation.reason: It is a two-block addition to a migration already being written, and it closes a gap the 5.1 plan left open.

Antigravity 1.5.1 carries only Opus/Sonnet 5.5 and Gemini ids. OpenCode already lists `opencode/claude-fable-5-2` through discovery. Codex and Gemini run non-Anthropic models.

sections.title: Confirm or override
sections.intro: Low-stakes defaults I'd bet on. One click each, or override with what it should be.

recommendation.value: `anthropic/claude-fable-5.2` — label 'Claude Fable 5.2', generic premium hint, `catalogOnly: true`, effort `[max, xhigh, high, medium, low, auto]`; update the 26→27 / 42→43 counts and the fx e2e exclusion list; no new positive e2e test.
recommendation.reason: Matches the Fable 5.1 row and the public Gateway's `reasoning_options`; catalogOnly is required because your signed-in catalog has no `anthropic/*` ids.

recommendation.value: One `CURSOR_MODEL_SPECS['claude-fable-5-2']` entry with the five plain effort ids, `supportsMaxMode: true`, no `fastEfforts`, no `-thinking-*` ids; no live Cursor spawn probe.
recommendation.reason: All five live labels contain '1M' and there are no thinking/fast variants; max mode is inferred from the labels (if rejected, one flag/test changes).

questions.title: No Claude Code CLI version floor for Fable 5.2

recommendation.value: Add no `MODEL_MIN_CLI_VERSION['claude-code']` entry; an older CLI fails at spawn on the unknown id.
recommendation.reason: Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5 deliberately added none; adding a 2.1.321 floor would also touch the exact-keys test.

recommendation.value: `bun run typecheck`; targeted `types` / `agents` / `effort-support` / `claude-local-setting` / `migrate` / `orchestrator-paste-withheld` tests; the existing self-deriving `e2e/fx-models.spec.ts`; then a full `bun test` (re-run known flaky tmux tests once).
recommendation.reason: Matches the repo's precedent for table-driven model additions; the e2e Claude picker assertion self-derives from `AGENT_OPTIONS`.
